subject: Order Form — IP & Model Improvement Limits (BrightByte)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BrightByte order form redlines — IP / product use focus

Team,

BrightByte sent back redlines on the MSA + Order Form this morning. Their highlights: they want broader downstream productization rights for outputs and a permissive clause to allow training on customer-provided content (they called it "improving their models"). They're also asking us to grant a feedback license that would let them use our product signals for their improvements.

I scanned the PDF (attached): main concern is they treat outputs as customer property without carving out our ability to use telemetry/feedback to operate and improve Redwood models. Legal will need to weigh in on both the output ownership language and the scope of any training/feedback license.

Attachments: BrightByte_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (redlines, inline comments)

Questions for this thread:
- What minimal language can we offer on outputs to avoid losing the ability to operate & improve our runtime?
- Can we accept customer productization of outputs so long as we retain anonymized telemetry/feedback rights?

Pls advise — I want to respond to Elaine by EOD with a clear proposal.

—Marcus
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte order form redlines — IP / product use focus

On Mon, Nov 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team,
> BrightByte sent back redlines...

Thanks for flagging. High-level legal stance and recommended language:

1) Outputs: we can allow BrightByte a broad, perpetual, non-exclusive right to use outputs they receive for their internal productization and downstream offerings, but must explicitly disclaim assignment of copyright/ownership to Redwood-generated outputs. Suggested sentence: "Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, and display Outputs for Customer's internal and customer-facing product features; nothing in this Agreement transfers ownership of Redwood's pre-existing models, service implementations, or intellectual property."

2) Training/data use: we should refuse a blanket training grant. Acceptable compromise: allow Customer to train customer-controlled models on Customer Content only if Customer explicitly opts in and warrants no PII; alternatively, permit Customer to submit anonymized/aggregated datasets for joint benchmarking under a separate SOW. We should preserve a carveout: Redwood will not use Customer Content for model training without opt-in.

3) Feedback license: we need a narrowly scoped license that allows Redwood to use aggregated, non-identifying telemetry and feedback signals to improve the Redwood service (not to claim ownership over Customer Content or Outputs). Suggested clause: "Redwood may analyze aggregated, de-identified usage data and feedback to improve its services; Redwood will not associate such data with Customer's identity or use Customer Content to train models unless Customer provides explicit written consent."

4) Ops & safety: propose an explicit sense that both parties will cooperate to remove PII and follow retention windows (30 days for raw telemetry, 12 months for aggregated metrics) — I'm flexible on exact numbers, but we need a retention/opt-out mechanism.

I've attached a draft marked-up Order Form that implements the above (see BrightByte_OrderForm_v3_redlines_marked.pdf). If Sales wants to offer a concession, we should limit it to: (a) allowing Customer to use Outputs for productization; (b) allowing Customer to opt-in for training rights under a separate schedule; (c) Redwood retains right to aggregated, de-identified feedback.

If you want speedy approval for a narrow concession to close the deal, I can sign-off on language that keeps Redwood's core protections.

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@brightbyte.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@brightbyte.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte Order Form comments (attached)

Elaine — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines attached. Forwarding our internal read and a proposed path forward.

Short summary of our proposed compromise:
- BrightByte: granted a perpetual, non-exclusive right to use Outputs for your internal products and customer features.
- Redwood: will NOT transfer ownership of Redwood models or code; Redwood retains rights to pre-existing IP.
- Training/Data: Redwood will NOT use Customer Content to train Redwood models without explicit opt-in language. If BrightByte wants training rights, we can scope it to Customer-provided, sanitized datasets under a separate SOW.
- Feedback: Redwood requests the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and feedback to operate and improve the Service; Redwood will not link telemetry to BrightByte's customer identity.

Can you confirm whether BrightByte can live with these guardrails? If not, please send specific suggested wording on training and feedback — we want to understand the use case (productization vs. model training) so we can bring a precise concession back.

Attached: summary + the PDF you sent (we preserved your numbering).

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@brightbyte.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@brightbyte.com>, contracts@brightbyte.com
Date: 2027-11-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte Order Form comments (attached)

Marcus — appreciate the clear summary and Laura's redline. A few clarifications from our side and a proposed compromise:

1) Outputs: BrightByte's ask is that Outputs produced from BrightByte Content be treated as Customer Outputs (we are not seeking ownership of Redwood's underlying models). The difference matters for our downstream licensing to our end customers — we need to be able to grant rights to Outputs in our own agreements.

2) Training: our primary requirement is the right to use Outputs to improve BrightByte's own models (not to train Redwood models). We are open to the opt-in approach you suggested but need this spelled out: BrightByte must be allowed to use Outputs for its internal model training and product improvement.

3) Feedback: BrightByte would like a reciprocal feedback pathway — if Redwood uses aggregated telemetry to improve service, BrightByte would like reasonable access to anonymized service analytics for debugging and integration purposes.

Proposed edits: add a sentence that allows Customer to "use Outputs for internal model training, provided Customer ensures Outputs do not contain PII and complies with applicable data protection laws"; and carve out that "Redwood may use de-identified telemetry for product improvement and share aggregated metrics with Customer to support integration".

I've attached a one-page marked proposal (BrightByte_training_feedback_proposal.pdf) showing our minimal changes. If we can get a short note agreeing to the above, our procurement team can accept the redlines and sign.

Best,
Elaine Cho
Head of Strategic Partnerships
BrightByte

Attached: BrightByte_training_feedback_proposal.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-02T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightByte Order Form comments — ops perspective

Looping in a quick ops perspective:

- Productization: allowing BrightByte to treat Outputs as "Customer Outputs" for their downstream customer contracts is reasonable, provided we add a short paragraph confirming that "Customer Outputs" do not include Redwood proprietary models, training weights, or service code. That protects our execs while removing an obstacle for BrightByte procurement.

- Training: BrightByte wants to train their own models on Outputs — that is fine. We should prohibit use of Customer Content (raw prompts, PII) for training Redwood models unless BrightByte explicitly opts in.

- Feedback and telemetry: Agree with Laura on an opt-out window and retention scheme. My recommended operational defaults: 30 days raw logs retention; 12 months for aggregated metrics; automated scrub of PII with an audit log. If BrightByte needs longer metrics retention we can add a paid telemetry package.

If Legal approves the language below, I'll prepare the final Order Form and follow up with DocuSign link:
"Redwood may analyze aggregated, de-identified usage metrics and feedback to improve its Services. Redwood will not use Customer Content to train its models without Customer's explicit written consent. Customer may use Outputs for its internal productization and to train Customer-controlled models provided Outputs are sanitized of PII and processed in compliance with applicable law."

—Ben
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-03T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Final sign-off: BrightByte IP & feedback concessions

Thanks for the threads and clear recs. I approve the following compromise to unblock BrightByte procurement, with narrow guardrails:

Approved language summary (for Order Form):
- Outputs: Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use Outputs for Customer's internal products and for downstream licensing to Customer's end users. This grant does not transfer ownership of Redwood's pre-existing models, code, or service implementations.

- Training: Customer may use Outputs to train Customer-controlled models. Redwood will not use Customer Content to train Redwood models without Customer's explicit, documented opt-in. Any data used for training must be sanitized; Customer warrants removal of PII and compliance with applicable law. Training on Outputs is permitted for Customer's own models only.

- Feedback/Telemetry: Redwood may process aggregated, de-identified usage metrics and feedback for the purpose of improving Redwood services. Raw logs containing PII will be retained for 30 days by default and then deleted unless Customer purchases extended telemetry retention. Redwood will provide BrightByte with aggregated analytics necessary for integration/debugging upon request.

Action items:
1) Marcus — send the updated Order Form to BrightByte with the above bullets reflected and the marked changes attached. Include the DocuSign link (use the short form) and request countersignature by EOD Friday.
2) Ben — prepare the operational addendum describing scrub/retention steps and the paid telemetry option.
3) Laura — please add the final legal paragraph and approve the redlined PDF for signature.

We should not concede any broader right for Redwood to train on Customer Content without an opt-in — that is a hard line. With these guardrails we can close.

-Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
